first.rationale: Two of the three pressures this quarter are funnel problems (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%), and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a single onboarding experiment plausibly touches both symptoms rather than one. memory_86 and memory_31 both point this way, and memory_91 suggests activation messaging is a complement rather than a substitute. I am choosing to verify memory_86 precisely because it is the load-bearing memory for this choice and its consolidated form only reports proxy outcomes — completion rate, time-to-value, 'early product adoption' — with no statement about qualified revenue or retention. Shortening onboarding can lift completion by removing qualification and data-capture steps while degrading lead quality downstream, which would move the metric and hurt the actual objective; I want the original record to see whether revenue-side outcomes were measured or merely assumed. The second pull goes to memory_73 because promotional pricing is the obvious reflex against a competitor's entry pricing and is the highest-risk option here: discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are the classic case where strong acquisition and revenue lift in-window conceals poor long-term qualified revenue, and the memory as consolidated says nothing about retention or margin horizon. If verification shows memory_73 was measured on durable revenue rather than acquisition, that materially changes the ranking; if it was not, I have a concrete reason to decline the reflex rather than just an instinct. I am not verifying memory_57 or memory_44 because referral incentives address neither current funnel decline, and enterprise sales-assist addresses a segment that is not the one under attack. Committing at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout: the inherited evidence is directionally credible but is summary-level and up to 64 days old, the competitive environment has since changed, and none of these memories were formed under current conditions. I will instrument on qualified-revenue and downstream conversion, not completion rate alone, so that a proxy win that does not convert is visible rather than banked. If the memory_86 pull reveals proxy-only measurement or a removed qualification step, I will narrow to a guarded test on a single self-serve cohort instead.

final.rationale:
The archive resolved both questions cleanly and in opposite directions. exp_86 held up better than its summary: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and critically 30-day retention +3%, so the win was not a proxy artifact bought by stripping qualification steps — the cohort that came through the shortened flow actually stuck. That is the evidence I needed to treat onboarding as a genuine lever on sustainable qualified revenue rather than a completion-rate cosmetic, and it addresses the upstream cause of both the -4% completion and, plausibly, part of the -6% activation decline. Committing the slot to simplify_onboarding.

exp_73 vindicates the decision to spend a pull on the reflex option. The consolidated memory said 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' and omitted 30-day retention -12% plus an explicit source-level instruction not to generalize targeted discounting as a sustainable-growth strategy. The acquired cohort does not survive first renewal. Against a competitor's entry pricing this was the obvious move and it would have been actively value-destroying under a long-term qualified-revenue objective — the +18% qualified revenue figure is measured inside a window that closes before the churn lands. Promotional pricing is off the table this week and I am recording the correction.

The wider lesson I am flagging for whoever inherits this: consolidation here has demonstrably dropped a load-bearing caveat and an explicit do-not-generalize warning while preserving the favorable numbers. memory_57 ('no measurable harm to retention'), memory_31, memory_91 and memory_44 are all still summary-level and may be similarly stripped — memory_57 in particular reads exactly like memory_73 did before verification. I am not treating any of them as settled, and memory_31 and memory_91 are supporting context for direction only, not licence to widen scope.

Holding at standard experiment rather than broad rollout despite the clean exp_86 record: that result is 24 days old, predates the competitive shift, and one verified prior does not license skipping measurement under changed conditions. Instrumentation is on downstream conversion, 30-day retention and qualified revenue, not completion rate — the failure mode exp_73 illustrates is precisely a headline metric moving while the cohort quality rots, and I want that visible in-flight. If retention or lead quality degrades against control I stop rather than scale.
